what: The logo (image or text) is read down to one dot per 11px cell, and random characters (10px monospace, cell 11×12) are stamped in the accent color on lit cells and the cell to their right, making a dot-character wordmark. Characters within 10 cells of the cursor are pushed away by up to (1 − distance/10)×7 cells and return (.1 per frame). Each press cycles through scatter (±10 cells, .075 each · each character 0~18 frames late) → falling to the floor (gravity .05 · bounce −.25) → returning to place (.05 each). A speech bubble, if present, follows the cursor to (+10,−14) at .18 per frame, hides while moving and pops out after a 140ms pause, and squashes to .82x when pressed then returns (320ms)

options.[data-fx-part=logo]: Logo (child) — If it is an image, it reads the opaque areas of that image, and if it is text, the area drawn in that font fitted to the panel width. Placed at the panel center at 100% width
options.[data-fx-part=bubble]: Speech bubble that follows the cursor (child, optional)

note: On touch devices (hover false) the canvas isn’t drawn and the logo is shown as it is. The original also shows a logo image below 1000px. It isn’t drawn while off screen.
